rootCauses: Outgoing shares contained only an app-required custom scheme, with no usable browser fallback.
Existing providerUrl was dropped by ProviderCatalogService before GraphQL/mobile, losing the exact public song page.
Track menus relied entirely on the bounded metadata registry, so an evicted song could lose its share entry despite retained player/list metadata.
Share button state alone was not a synchronous duplicate guard; delayed lookup/navigation needed lifecycle and identity validation.
implemented: Nullable public shareUrl projected from the existing MusicProvider providerUrl through Track and CatalogSong GraphQL types; no database schema or identity change.
Dedicated authenticated metadata query checks exact canonical ID and fresh availability before sharing, without changing normal discovery/playback queries.
Native share title/text contain actual title/artist, exact provider HTTPS song page and exact canonical-ID Fav Music deep link; playback URLs and credentials are rejected.
Same-song share requests coalesce; conflicting requests report busy; stale/unmounted requests cannot open a delayed native sheet.
Track menu fallback uses the actual selected player/list track when registry metadata is evicted; all normal track menus reuse the same sharing action.
Incoming custom links remain protected by real authentication; exact IDs are looked up for review. Loading, retry, missing songs, identity substitution and stale account/payload results are handled.
Play from shared review waits for the intended queue and guards against duplicate/wrong/stale navigation; opening a link never automatically plays or saves.
Existing Android text-share ingress recognizes one validated track deep link in addition to existing reel ingress.

Sorry, this song was not found. is used for missing tracks and completed current InstaMus manual searches with zero matches/no further pages; loading, failed, stale and partial searches are not called missing.
